input: # ES5.1 escapes JSON5 accepts: a NonEscapeCharacter yields itself, and
# \uXXXX surrogate halves combine into one code point.
# EscapeCharacter includes DecimalDigit, so \1..\9 (legacy octal) are
# not escapes; `\0` is one only when NOT followed by a digit. `\u{...}`
# A digit after a COMPLETED escape is just a character.
# A LineContinuation belongs to the STRING grammar only: it is stripped
# inside a string literal, and is not a token separator anywhere else.
# --- Retired divergences, now agreed by both ports -----------------------
# These nine inputs stood in test/divergent.tsv until 2026-08-20, when the
# engine repairs landed and every row went red. They are here so both
# suites keep EXECUTING them: a retired row whose input survives only in a
# comment enforces nothing, and if both ports regressed identically the
# P3 (parser#139) — the TypeScript escape decode used parseInt as a
# validator, stopped at the first non-hex character and INVENTED a
# character never in the input. It now requires the full fixed-width hex
# run. Both ports, and both the sibling and the pinned engine, reject
# P1/P2 (parser#128) — a quote used to end a Go text run and did not end a
# TypeScript one, so Go raised unterminated_string where TypeScript raised
# The code is deliberately NOT pinned here. This fixture is shared, and it

# release, so against go.mod's parser the Go port still says
# unterminated_string. A bare ERROR is true of both, and still fails if
